items.label: Fig. 2, power of epiForest (24 bars)

assumptions.what: Published bars and box medians read off Figs 2 and 3 (the 2400 x 1200 images in the paper's PDF) through each panel's tick marks
assumptions.sensitivity: Tick fits within 0.22 px; one power point is 3.82 px and every bar reads within 0.2 points of an integer count; Fig. 3 medians within 0.1 of a half-integer. The reading error is far below the Monte Carlo tolerance.

assumptions.what: Disease models: Marchini et al.'s tables of odds for models 1 and 3; for model 2 the table of epiMODE (Tang et al. 2009, the same group), (1+t)^2, (1+t)^3, (1+t)^4 for two, three and four disease alleles, where Marchini has 1+t, (1+t)^2, (1+t)^4
assumptions.sensitivity: Chosen among six documented readings by the exact chi-squared power, which involves no random forest (output/checks/model_variants.json): epiMODE's table puts 21 of the 24 chi-squared bars within Monte Carlo error (8 of 8 in model 2); Marchini's table 17 (4 of 8); either table read as relative risks 18, and Marchini's model 2 at MAF 0.05 to 0.2 cannot reach lambda = 0.5 as relative risks.

assumptions.what: The marginal effect lambda is the odds ratio of the marginal penetrances of the heterozygote and the wild-type homozygote, minus 1 (Zhang and Liu 2007; epiMODE Text S1); prevalence 0.1 for every model (the paper)
assumptions.sensitivity: Prevalence 0.01 for model 2 (epiMODE's setting) puts 15 or 18 of the 24 chi-squared bars within Monte Carlo error instead of 21 (model_variants.json).

assumptions.what: LD between a disease locus and its marker: the marker has the locus's minor allele frequency and each marker allele follows the locus allele on its haplotype with correlation r = sqrt(r2) (epiMODE Text S1); null markers have MAF from U(0, 0.5) (the paper); the two disease markers sit at random columns
assumptions.sensitivity: Using 0.7 as r instead of r2 lowers model 3 at MAF 0.5 to 9% chi-squared power against the published 38% (model_variants.json, epimode_odds_r2_as_r: 19 of 24 bars within Monte Carlo error).

assumptions.what: A disease marker counts as identified when it is in any reported test; power is the share of 100 data sets where both are
assumptions.sensitivity: summary.json gives epiForest's power when both markers must be in one reported test (epiforest_joint) or reported singly (epiforest_one_way).

assumptions.what: ntree = 500 (randomForest's default) for the first forest and every SWSFS forest; the paper gives ntree only for the AMD forests (10^6)
assumptions.sensitivity: With 2000 trees SWSFS keeps still fewer SNPs on the data sets we tried (output/checks/swsfs_variants.json).

assumptions.what: mtry = floor(sqrt(number of SNPs in the forest)), randomForest's default (the paper prints the default garbled)
assumptions.sensitivity: With mtry fixed at 31 for every SWSFS forest: output/checks/swsfs_variants.json.

assumptions.what: B statistic with pseudo-counts 0.5 and P0 in the denominator (the paper prints P1/P1); 2B minus a shift from Stirling's expansion is chi-squared with 3^k - 1 degrees of freedom (3^k - 3^t conditional); the conditional B tests the other markers with the reported ones keeping their association
assumptions.sensitivity: On null data the shifted statistic has the right mean and tail for one- and two-way tests and is conservative for three-way tests (check.bstat_null).

assumptions.what: Bonferroni over all L = 1000 markers (L, L(L-1)/2, L(L-1)(L-2)/6), as the paper says
assumptions.sensitivity: summary.json, epiforest_bonf_candidates: Bonferroni over the candidates instead.

cause.summary: 15 of 24 bars within Monte Carlo error. Where the signal is weak (r2 = 0.7, models 2 and 3, MAF 0.05 to 0.2) ours is higher, as our chi-squared is in model 3; where the paper's epiForest is far ahead of chi-squared (models 2 and 3, r2 = 1, MAF 0.05 and 0.1) ours is lower: 2 against 16, 38 against 57, 87 against 97, 72 against 89. There our first forest ranks a disease marker low (model 2, MAF 0.05: the lower one at rank 800 in median), so neither SWSFS nor the B tests see it. The paper's forest settings are not given; mtry = 100 ranks the markers higher at MAF 0.1 but not at MAF 0.05.

hypotheses.hypothesis: SWSFS keeps fewer SNPs than the paper's (fig3.medians), so disease markers fall outside the candidates
hypotheses.test: summary.json, upper bounds on power if both markers within the top i = k + w or the top 46: model 2, r2 = 1, MAF 0.05 to 0.2: 2, 41, 93 and 1, 38, 92 against 16, 57, 97; model 3, r2 = 1, MAF 0.05: 77 against 89

hypotheses.hypothesis: Another setting of the first forest ranks the disease markers higher: genotypes as numbers 0/1/2, 2000 trees, or mtry = 100
hypotheses.test: rank_variants.R, 12 data sets per setting (the study's setting reproduces the study's ranks in 48 of 48): both markers in the top 46 in 0 of 12 for every setting at model 2, r2 = 1, MAF 0.05; at MAF 0.1 in 8 of 12 with mtry = 100 against 1 to 3 of 12 otherwise

hypotheses.hypothesis: Another rule for a disease marker being identified
hypotheses.test: summary.json variants: both in one reported test 8 of 24 bars within error, both reported singly 17, Bonferroni over the candidates only 7

hypotheses.hypothesis: Model 3 at small MAF simulated stronger than in the paper (the open cause of fig2.chisq): our chi-squared power is above the paper's in the same settings
hypotheses.test: compare.py: chi-squared 26, 72, 99 against 0, 11, 79 (model 3, r2 = 0.7, MAF 0.05 to 0.2) and 64 against 48 (r2 = 1, MAF 0.05)

items.label: Fig. 2, power of BEAM (24 bars)

cause.summary: BEAM 1.0 (Zhang and Liu 2007) was distributed only as a binary from the authors' Harvard page, which now answers 403; the Pasteur mirror keeps only its README, and the Wayback Machine could not be reached from this session. assumptions.what: Stepwise logistic regression: 100 SNPs (10%) kept by their single-locus likelihood-ratio test (2 df, adjusted by L); stage 2 tests every pair and triple of kept SNPs for interaction, the logistic model with one parameter per observed genotype combination against the model with main effects only (4 df for a pair, 20 for a triple), adjusted by L(L-1)/2 and L(L-1)(L-2)/6 as the paper adjusts epiForest's tests; a disease marker is found in any significant test. assumptions.sensitivity: Chosen among five readings by the number of published bars within Monte Carlo error (comparison.json, sensitivity.fig2): this one 17 of 24; interaction terms adjusted by the number of stage-2 tests 14; the full model against the null model (Marchini's two-stage strategy) 4 adjusted by the stage-2 tests and 8 by all tests; single-locus tests alone 19. The full-model readings find a disease marker through its main effect in stage 2, which the single-locus test missed, and run 20 to 70 points above the paper.

cause.summary: With the reading that fits best (interaction terms in stage 2, adjusted by all tests; found by search) 17 of 24 bars within Monte Carlo error.
